originalGeneration.skillDescription: Silence Sever. Show one merciless cut-line ripping through darkness toward a bright weak point, with fine silver splinters and a fading afterimage trailing behind it. The frame should feel quiet just before impact, not explosive or theatrical. Strong single kill-line cut silhouette first. Favor kill-windows, cuts in the dark, venom residue, and vanishing pressure over heroic symmetry or loud elemental blasts. The frame should stay dark and predatory; bright accents must feel like a strike-point or venom glint, never like a radiant core.
originalGeneration.presentationStyle: pure effect icon. No character. Focus on the magical or physical effect itself as a clean standalone icon.
originalGeneration.primaryRequest: Create 1 RPG skill icon arranged in a 1x1 grid on a single image. The icon should fill the square and read clearly as a standalone skill icon. Keep the design simple and not overly complex, but allow layered internal detail inside one strong main shape. Use a color palette predominantly consisting of obsidian black, bruised violet, poisoned crimson, smoky graphite, cold silver pinpoints. The icon should visually represent a assassin finishing strike, evoking lethal execution, shadow speed, venom pressure, and fatal target isolation, with bold, clean, premium RPG readability and a clearly dominant focal silhouette. Avoid generic spell blobs, undirected glow, centered orb-only compositions, and off-class substitute motifs. Do not add an outer card frame, decorative border, or UI plate around the icon. Avoid overly abstract swirls, orb-only compositions, shapeless glow masses, and generic magical blobs. Prefer one concrete, class-appropriate central subject or one clearly readable cause-and-effect moment.

Skill description: Silence Sever. Show one merciless cut-line ripping through darkness toward a bright weak point, with fine silver splinters and a fading afterimage trailing behind it. simplifiedGeneration.prompt:
Create a simplified skill icon from the viewed source image.

Keep the same skill identity as the source. Preserve the main object or magic effect, dominant colors, direction of motion, composition, and the most recognizable silhouette.

Human silhouette rule: if the source image includes a person, face, body, hand, weapon-wielding pose, or humanoid action figure, keep that human element as a simplified silhouette. Use a clear dark-or-lit cutout, partial bust, head-and-shoulder shape, hand/weapon cue, or compact action pose. Reduce facial detail, clothing detail, anatomy detail, and small accessories, but do not remove the person when the person is part of the original image. If the source has no person, do not add one.

Layering rule: when both a character and a skill effect are visible, keep the character silhouette as the main readable anchor and simplify the effect into 1 to 3 supporting shapes around it. The icon should still read as the same source image at small size.

Differentiation rule: avoid making skills in the same class look like the same generic orb, burst, slash, arrow, or glow. Each icon must keep one distinctive motif from the source image, such as a unique pose, weapon angle, projectile shape, rune shape, plant shape, shield shape, machine part, or color accent.

Style constraints: square 1:1 game icon, no text, no numbers, no logo, no frame or border, centered subject, bold simple silhouette, 3 to 6 large readable shapes, reduced particles, reduced micro-detail, clean edge highlights, compact glow, high contrast, polished fantasy game UI, simple background aura only when it helps readability. Simplify detail, but prioritize source similarity over uniform style.
